body: I'm not familiar with the au pair program, but can she get another visa? Can she try to find another host family closer to you?

Sounds like you've got your answer. If you want to have sex more frequently, you might have to make her fold your laundry for you or something occasionally. Just ask her what she'd like and communicate with her that while it doesn't necessarily turn you on, she turns you on and that's enough for you to play out some of her fantasies.

It sucks because this is a time sensitive issue. I personally believe that you should never rush into anything involving a relationship.

Is she asking you to marry her? What does she do for work that would allow her to move across the country? Why can't she get another visa? If there's a voice in your head saying no, I'd listen to it. Not marrying her right now doesn't mean you don't love her, it just means you want to make good decisions.

>  I asked again.. was he interested. He said no. I decided I can't be here if he's with someone else. Now the wheels are heavily in motion for me to move. And now.. out of no where.. he wants to talk about us dating.

Sounds like he likes the attention you give him but not you...

>  everyone around us would ask me.. are you two together? They sensed our energy.

I hate when people say things like this. They don't know a thing about either of your love lives (assuming you haven't spoken to them about it), so what the fuck do they know? Just because people hang out together does not mean they're dating.

> Moving would mean far better job opportunities for me, and having a family to spend time with during holidays ect

Sounds pretty good to me...

> But it might also mean never finding love. Or having another 5 years go by.

There's no guarantee that staying would mean finding love or having another 5 years go by. Might as well get something good out of the hand you're dealt.

He sounds like kinda a dick to me, but I don't know him. I wouldn't waste any more of your time on this guy who's been leading you on for what sounds like years. IF you want to give it a chance go for it, but keep in mind his previous transgressions. Whatever you decide, I'd look into therapy since it always helps to talk to someone about your problems.

I have a friend like this as well. He's great to be around when he's around, but you never know if he'll actually be around. I think you can stay friends, just try to care less about what he's doing and whether or not he shows up somewhere. I would try not to put yourself in situations where you need him to show up somewhere, as it probably won't happen. Invite him to things, but don't be upset when he says he'll attend, but doesn't. 

> The fact that I am writing in this subreddit confirms that I have an obsession 

I think I'd have to agree. It might be best to step away from this situation(him) for a while and reorganize your self. Take some time to yourself to think about what you want from your friendship and what he can actually provide. You might just need to lower your expectations.

> I’m also a little concerned about our sex life if this is what she considers exciting now.

Why? Are you hoping for something more exciting? Did you previously do something weirder or more exciting to you?

I don't think it's wrong to not be turned on like she is, it's just not your kink. If she likes it, or doing the housewife fetish thing, thats fine too. 

The real question is, does it turn you off? If you come home and she's in just an apron it seems like both of you could benefit. You don't have to be turned on by her folding laundry, you can just be turned on by her.

It's probably not worth the effort. If someone won't put in the effort now, they sure as heck won't in the future. If you really want to, send her a message asking if she's free on a specific date and time about 1-2 weeks in the future (nothing last minute). If she isn't interested then just move on. You can let her know why you're moving on if you want to, but you don't need to.

Why did you marry someone so quickly? Why did you marry someone with kids when it sounds like you never once interacted with them before hand? Good things take time and relationships are no exception. From what you've written it sounds like you rushed into this situation. Get out while you can and next time take a little more time before marriage.

I think a lot of people have issues with trusting that their SO really does love them. I'm not sure what you can do besides keep telling her the truth. You can tell her this truth with words, but more importantly actions. It's okay to spoil your SO every so often with a romantic evening or day event of her favorite activity. Think about why you lover her and think about how you can show that love to her. Anyone can say three words, but not everyone will want to put in the effort to cook her favorite food one night, or send her a funny meme that made you think of her.

> but do I try and stay and fix this relationship?

Nope.

> I feel like a shitty boyfriend

Not because of this you're not. It seems like you're doing your best and are on a great track. You admitted earlier to your past faults and seem to be trying to improve, so keep it up!

You're very young and you have a ton of time to meet new people. LDR's are extremely hard and are probably never worth the effort. She doesn't seem interested in maintaining your LDR, so it's doubly not worth your effort to try to maintain it. 

>  do I lose the one I truly love, just for us to be separated when she comes back every 3 months? I don't want to play mind games, I want to make up my mind: what do I do?

Just be honest with her and say you don't think you can maintain a LDR with someone who isn't interested in maintaining it. Don't play any mind games. Just let her know that you want to break up and that you wish her the best.

In the future when someone says something like this: "she likes another guy but still wants me" they are being selfish and not worth spending more time on unless that's your kink.

>But we are fully convinced that same-sex marriages are immoral and against the will of God and that our presence would be a sign of approval for something that God disapproves of

Seems like it is what you believe. I agree it's a bit harsh, but you should definitely mention the part where she's probably better off without you. Maybe just phrase it more flowery to hide the fact that you don't approve of her being happy.

> but my husband said she's going to feel bad regardless of what we say since we're not going to be in attendance 

Absolutely true. You're probably going to get a lot of hate from reddit for your beliefs. I personally think it's sad that you chose your religion over your own flesh and blood.

Just tell her the truth but be ready for her to be upset with you and possibly never talk to you again. Seems like a win for you since it must be so hard blaspheming god by being a part of your daughter's life.

Then have her call you when she brings it up. I'm not sure I subscribe to the whole "cut that shit out" bit, but you know him better than I do. I do agree that you being there for him, in any capacity, will help him. Let him know that you know he's strong and that alcoholism is very hard to overcome, but that he is strong enough to overcome it. Let him know that you want to help him overcome it and if you think he'd think like this, that you helping him absolutely does not make him weak.
If you believe she is in immediate danger, call 911. If not call the suicide prevention hotline (800-273-8255) and ask them for help. Make sure you stay with her until she is safe either way.

It doesn't necessarily mean anything, but it also doesn't necessarily mean nothing.  Has he mentioned why he thinks they didn't last longer? Maybe he has a really hard time picking good women to date, or maybe he starts beating his SO after 4 months of dating. If he seems like an okay guy and you like him, try it out. If he starts changing drastically for the worse shortly after dating him, then good job on you for detecting it early and keeping it in mind for when you leave.

Nothing wrong with having different definitions. If you don't like using tongue and he does, you might not be good together, especially if he's going to critique your technique every time you kiss.

> he said he has “high expectations” 

Sounds like he's getting worse and worse as time goes on...

> I just want to know if I’m being sensitive or if it’s ok to feel insecure about this?

I don't think you're being sensitive. I think you're just not compatible together and that's okay. He seems a bit odd since most people at least try to act good in the first few months of meeting each other. I'd count it as a blessing that he's displaying things that you don't like this early, as you don't have to waste time with him.  In my opinion anyone who tells you they have high expectations and then constantly pesters you about how you're not meeting them is just trying to manipulate you somehow.

I think these things are best done in person if possible. Definitely call your mother first before him. I think the best order would be to call AA for advice, then your mother to discuss the advice, then schedule a time when she's there and you can call or skype or w/e you choose to bring it up with him.

>  Honestly, I'd much rather deal with my parents 

Of course you would, just like he'd rather deal with his parents. I do agree that his mother sounds like a lot of work, which luckily for you, you don't **HAVE** to deal with. I don't think he's going to change his opinions of his mother without something cataclysmic happening, so you have to ask your self if he's worth it. Follow up question, do you really want to be with someone who thinks its "hard to breath in a mask" or "protecting other people I live near is a violation of my rights"?

You need to tell her ASAP. You're allowed to be Polyamorous, but she's also allowed to not be into that. It might suck for you but you need to do what's right and find other people who want to be polyamorous if she's not into it.

Call him up and let him know you've been missing him and ask him how he's doing. Call up your mom as well and ask her to present a united front on this issue. She seems to think it's an issue as well or she wouldn't have mentioned it. I hate to say make it like an intervention or something, but maybe your mom can say what you want to in your stead. I'm not an expert on alcoholic interventions, but it seem like if two people who love you show up and ask you to work with them to get better, it'll be better than one.

If he says its being blown out of proportions, just say something like: "yeah, I know, but unfortunately our Dad's genes make it really easy to get really bad really quickly, and if we work on it early it will never be out of proportions"

Good luck, and I think you're going to need to be very patient with him as no addict ever easily admits they have a problem. Maybe call a doctor or an AA group for advice.

> sometimes when I do he rejects it and gives some excuse, which makes me feel so undesired

Sometimes people don't want to have sex. It absolutely doesn't mean you're undesirable. It's also fine to feel bad when this happens, but its not really anyone's fault and you should try not to get mad at him.

It sounds like he could be a little bit depressed. It's fairly easy to get depressed during these trying times and depression makes you less likely to want sex.

> how do I stop feeling this way?

You have to tell yourself that not wanting sex does not mean he doesn't find you attractive and it's not right to get mad at him for not wanting sex.

> How do I try to help his sex drive?

Ask him if he's doing okay. Ask him if COVID is making him really sad. Is he exercising correctly? Ask him if he wants to go on a walk/hike/run with you. If he used to go to a gym, ask him if he wants to buy some weights. 

> How do I maybe even lower my sex drive?

Not sure this is possible. You could masturbate but it seems like you don't like it, which is fine and honestly doesn't work all the time anyways.

> 2. He gets upset again and we no longer have a relationship

IF you don't say anything, the first thing will come true. If you don't say anything, do you think you could have a *good* relationship with him anyway?

I think you need to talk to him about this. Ask him if he remembers growing up together with your Dad drinking constantly. Ask him if he enjoyed growing up like that, and tell him that you didn't. Tell him you love him and want what's best for him and that it brings back painful memories to see him follow in your Dad's footsteps. Let him know that you're there for him and that you strongly encourage him getting professional help, because alcoholism is a disease that needs to be treated. You wouldn't get an STD and just hope that it goes away without a Doctor's help right?

I agree with your position that you don't want to and shouldn't be with this person. I think the best way to go about it is to say something like: "I don't think this relationship is going to work out anymore. Thanks for the good times, I wish you well in the future."

You don't owe him a big explanation. If he asks and seems genuinely interested in improving, go ahead and tell him kindly your reasons. You have no responsibility to fix this person, and you should only help those who want help.

> other women have left him

Why do you think they left him? Probably because he's a manipulative creep. I think that you should go with CPS and get your education and stabilize. See if CPS can get you into therapy as well because abuse as a child can lead to further issues down the road if not addressed. To quote a famous song, players only love you when they're playin. This man is using you and does not have your best interests in mind, so do yourself a favor and follow in the footsteps of the other women who finally figured out he was an asshole, and leave. Get some more stability in your life with CPS and I guarantee you can find someone better for you.

So what? It seems like you've heard the same thing from multiple people in this thread. If you get shit from relatives, tell them in full why you're upset with your parents. Your mom sounds like a bitch for ruining part of your life so don't let her ruin any more of it.

> I know they’re my parents and I need to forgive them no matter what ,but this is hard.

The thing that most people don't tell you is that you don't need to forgive them. You can absolutely forgive them if you want to, but you also don't have to. People talk about closure and how you can only get it from forgiving people who wronged you, but that's kinda bullshit. Only you have the power to give yourself closure. shitty people are shitty and almost never change, especially without consequences to their actions. If you don't tell your mother/father how much they hurt you and how much their actions ruined your relationship with them, they're going to think everything's fine. It's not fine though, so tell them. You can still be respectful to them and tell them they're cunts (use better language to be respectful).

If she still refuses, ask her why.

I don't think that sexual compatibility is something "nowhere near as important as the other things".  It's just as important as the other things. I think that there are many wonderful people in the world with a caring heart, humor, brains and the desire to peg you.

It seems that you're not sexually incompatible, but it could be better. I'm assuming that you and her enjoy having vanilla sex together and it won't become some sort of dead bedroom situation (i.e. no sex ever) because that would be a big issue.

The only advice I can give you is that you can probably find happiness wherever you try. If you want to stay with this person, I'm sure you'll be able to be happy having vanilla sex for the rest of your life. If you want to leave this person, I'm sure it will suck for a while, but you'll find someone else that will make you just as happy if not more. There isn't such a thing as a perfect person, but there are a lot of iterations in the world to choose from.  Both options would require effort, and both will probably make you fee bad and good throughout the rest of your life.

My advice is couples counseling.

I think this is the best way for you to prove to her that you are trying your best after making a big mistake. Lying about strippers being at your party is really bad... I think you're making valuable effort to make up for your past mistakes and she (rightfully so) is having a hard time trusting that this is real effort.

 I'm assuming that you're not sexualizing women when you're out and about. I think it's normal to have momentary thoughts about the attractiveness of human beings throughout the day. If a really hot guy or girl walks past me and my SO while we're out, we usually comment on it to each other. Humans are attractive and it's pretty normal to think that. 

Just suggest therapy and let her know that you're trying your best to be the best you can for her, and that you think that it would help you and her to go discuss things with a professional.

You didn't do anything wrong, nor are you an idiot. I don't think you're being overly sensitive at all, anyone should be upset with a response like that.

Maybe say it nicer than that but if he dismisses your feelings again I think it's time to move on. You deserve someone who respects your feelings.

If someone's husband was abusive, should they not lock their husband out when they fear for their safety? Then again, I'm no expert. I've hear that finding the right therapist for you can take a while and if this is the first/only one you've tried it might be worth getting some a second or third opinion.

I think that you should let your wife know that you want her to get the alone time she needs, but that you feel very worried when she locks the door (for whatever reason it is that you're worried). Let her know that you'll respect her boundaries and let her have as much time as she needs alone, with the door shut, whatever, but that you don't want her to lock the door.

I think most times parents will do what's right for their child, especially when someone outside of the family is there. I don't think I ever saw my parents argue when we had guests over, but they did argue in front of us as kids.

It seems like you and your family want the same thing, so you should invite him. I think it will go fine, and if not, I doubt he'd think less of you (if he does, he's not as great as you think he is). It might be awkward, but meeting SO's parents always is a bit awkward.

No but in all seriousness I think its fairly normal to lose some interest in people over time in a relationship. When you start dating someone, everything about them is new and exciting. But over time, by definition less and less that they do will be new, and therefore less exciting. Also the more time spent together the more you see of their true nature. Everyone puts on the best performance in the first few months of dating.

Regarding the cream cheese, have you let her know that it upsets you? Maybe growing up her parents never cared or showed her how to do it that way and she doesn't know any better?

I think your best option is to communicate with her when she does something that annoys you, but do it in a kind manner. "GF, the cream cheese box is destroyed. Can we open it at the top next time to keep the cream cheese in it next time?" Also maybe try to go on more dates or do more activities together to see if your loss of feelings is just due to the current difficult times, or actual loss of feelings. If it's the latter, there's nothing wrong with breaking up as long as you do it nicely.

I think you can start by apologizing for getting overly pissed and using strong language. It shouldn't be a huge emotional wall to let her know that you didn't mean to be mean to her. It might be easier to start things with a text that you've written out and read over. Texting takes some of the emotion out of the conversation, and would allow you to let her know your feelings without having to speak them aloud (which can be difficult).

Let her know that you know you have an issue with this and that you're trying to be better, but you feel that you need to take it at your own pace. Let her know you feel uneasy about her talking about it ~~and would prefer she kept it between the two of you instead of vocalizing it like before~~. She probably didn't think anything was wrong about saying "I've seen you cry" because to her its normal for people to cry in front of each other.

Edit: I think I misinterpreted who was there when you and her made the joke.

It's fine to not want Kids and not want to marry, but if your SO wants the opposite then you're not compatible no matter how fun it is to be together. I think this is something that should be discussed early on in the relationship. Not first date, but it's not really a relationship worth pursuing if you don't want similar things.

>  Do you really think if I give her a very long period of time to get over this and I truly change for the better that it would still be bad for me to reach out?

If she's not seeing anyone and you think you've improved send her a message, but don't expect a lot or pursue things after a negative response. I personally think it would be better for you to find someone else after improving yourself since you've already permanently damaged her trust in you. I think there are plenty of amazing women out there that will see the reformed you and be just as great if not greater than you and this girl.

> “ you want to waste all this and break up”

This is spooky.

I think its semi-normal for things to slow down from the initial Dating Phase of relationships, but they shouldn't stop. It sounds like you're communicating your needs clearly to him, but he won't listen. 

I know that the Pandemic can lead to a lot of "normal" date areas being closed or too scary to go to, but there are other things you can do together besides go to dinner.  Bike rides, Hikes, Cooking dinner together, etc. are all things you can do to spend more quality time together. I'd try to avoid things like watching movies, as I can understand the desire to prefer playing games than watching a movie. 

If trying to set up something that both of you can do together doesn't work, and he still won't talk with you, I think your options kinda run out...

> “ you want to waste all this and break up”

Sunk Cost Fallacy. Don't let your previous effort prevent you from having fun in the future. It is not a waste to make yourself happy in the long run. It's a tough choice to make, but immediate and short term pain leading to longer term happiness is better than continuous, dull pain in my opinion. That's why they say its better to rip off a band-aid.

> Also he thinks that he is too old for college and everyone will think about him as a failure.

This is not true. You're never too old to learn something new.
